$comment: Canvas hashes at fixed states. Regenerate with the Copy new baseline button in widgets/_lab/fingerprint.html, and commit the new baseline in the SAME commit as the change that moved the rendering. Two kinds of state: a SETTLED one passes shown= so the figure is fully built and nothing is moving; a DRIVEN one carries drive={click,frames,dt} and the harness supplies the frame clock by hand, so a mid-animation frame is exactly as reproducible as a settled one. A suite of settled states alone is no test of the animation at all — that gap once let every falling ball sit six columns off-centre while all eight settled states matched. Confirm a new driven state is identical across three runs before recording it. Hashes are viewport-dependent: the harness renders into a fixed 900px frame, so do not change FRAME_W without regenerating.

DRIVEN, REGRESSION: TWO step clicks. The counter was named anim.done, which core reads as "finished" and answers with Replay — so every click after the first reset the widget instead of advancing it, and it sat at one study forever. Play masked it entirely, because one click runs to the end. No single click reaches this state.
The default: the flat carpet against its m/20 rule, then the same genes after each correction. 1094 called, 21, 75.
NOT ONE GENE IS DIFFERENT, and about 1000 still come back at p < 0.05 — every one a false positive. The setting the widget exists for.
POWER: a moderate 0.9 SD effect is invisible to correction at n = 12 and largely recovered at n = 60. Guards the raised n ceiling.
DRIVEN: mid-batch, with the corrections computed on the genes tested so far.
DRIVEN, REGRESSION: TWO step clicks. A counter named anim.done made every click after the first replay instead of advance, and Play hid it completely. No single click reaches this state.

The Both tab, climb finished. The only contour in the suite, and the only right-angled path over one.
n = 60 with the factor row off: the count axis has ratcheted out and the exponent has collapsed. Catches anything that scales with n.
A near-Poisson population (size 8) at small n. The size tab should find little to fix here, so it guards the branch that reports it.

Binomial, settled. The attempts strip at rest and the theory dots over the pile.
Hypergeometric drawing 60% of the pool — the case where without-replacement bites.
Poisson, settled. Half of the pair: a rate that never moves, var/mean at 1.
Negative binomial on the SAME axis as the Poisson above — the pair's whole point.

Exponential: the gap mechanism, marking the wait between the Poisson's own arrivals.
R code on the Poisson: four cards, each led by the question its function answers.
R code on a narrowed uniform, where dunif reads 5.0 — a density above 1, on a slider.

The setup at the default: two curves, the line at 1.645, alpha and beta before any data.
Effect None: the two curves coincide exactly, and 5% still lands past the line.
n = 100 on the RAW axis, where sample size narrows BOTH curves — the motion z hides.
The test-statistic axis: the line pinned at 1.645 and only the alternative sliding.
alpha 0.001 against a small effect — alpha chosen, beta inherited, and beta is nearly all of it.
1000 studies run: the observed rates against the predicted ones they were told to check.
The null, fully run: 5% of studies significant at every n, which is what alpha MEANS.
Underpowered and fully run: a small effect at n=12, where most studies miss it.
Expected shape off, so the pile stands alone against the line.

Design at rest with an effect and 1:4 enrolment — the dot scale derived from the fullest box.

Odds ratio, cohort, 40/20: the survivors stepped aside and the claim names the overstatement.

Nobody died in either arm: 0/0, undefined rather than infinite, and the figure says so.

The fit tab at twelve parameters: the training curve through the noise and the held-out error already climbing. The state the widget exists to reach.
The cross-validation tab, five folds. The aqua fold mark only exists here, so no fit-tab state covers it.
Two parameters — a straight line — with both roles drawn and the true curve revealed. Covers `look=both` (no error lines) and the afterDrive reveal in one state.
DRIVEN: mid-add, one parameter going onto the ladder. A settled state is blind to anything drawn only while the curve is moving.
The opening state: both dials at zero, so this IS plain linear regression and all thirteen coefficients are in.
Lasso at a1 = 1. Three of thirteen survive, and the other ten bars are EXACTLY zero — the one thing no other setting shows.
Elastic net at both dials wide open, on the most elongated pair (Weight against Hip, 5.73:1). The grouping effect puts coefficients back.

The near-circular end of the pair range: Age against Weight, r = 0.013, contours 1.01:1 — where the diamond and the circle become the same shape. Also the only cover the rail matrix gets, since the rail is outside both hashes: it proves the parameter reaches the figure, not that the cell sets it.
